card.title: Point at any commit
card.blurb: Name a commit without its hash, and stand on one directly. Count backwards with `main~2` and `HEAD~1`, put a branch on an older commit, and see what a detached `HEAD` looks like.
hero.title: Point at any commit
intro.0: Every command so far has meant `where I am now`. To reach an older commit the obvious move is to copy its hash out of `git log` - seven characters to read carefully and retype without slipping. Git will count backwards for you instead: `HEAD~1` is one step back, `main~2` is two. Here you use those names to put a branch further back, and to stand on an older commit yourself.
task.1.title: Put a name on an older commit
task.1.context:
`main` names the newest commit on that line. Add `~` and a number and git walks back that many parents, so `main~1` is the commit just before the tip.

`git branch old <rev>` puts the name `old` wherever that revision lands, and leaves you standing where you are. You work out the number from the log.
task.1.goal.0: Read `git log --oneline` and count how many steps back `add dog` sits from the tip.
task.1.goal.1: Check the count with `git rev-parse main~<n>` before you use it.
task.1.goal.2: Put a branch called `old` on that commit with `git branch old main~<n>`, and stay on `main`.
task.2.title: Stand on a commit, not a branch
task.2.context:
`git checkout` takes the same kind of name. Point it at an older commit and there is no branch sitting there, so `HEAD` ends up on the commit itself. Git calls that a detached `HEAD`.

Counting starts from where you stand, so `HEAD~1` is the commit before this one. Read the log again to find the number you need.
task.2.goal.0: Read `git log --oneline` and find the commit whose message is `add bird`.
task.2.goal.1: Count the steps back from the tip and step onto it with `git checkout HEAD~<n>`.
task.2.goal.2: Read `git status` - it should say `HEAD detached`. `main` does not move.
task.3.title: Point at any commit - recap
task.3.context: Names that count backwards, and what happens when you stand where no branch is.
task.3.summaryIntro: A hash is one way to name a commit, and usually the least convenient one. `HEAD` and a branch name are the other two, and both take a step-back suffix - so most of the time you never have to read a hash at all.
task.3.summaryItems.0.title: Revision -
task.3.summaryItems.0.text: any way of naming a commit: `HEAD`, a branch, a tag, a hash, or a step back from one of them.
task.3.summaryItems.1.title: `~n` -
task.3.summaryItems.1.text: walks back n parents, so `HEAD~1` is the commit before the one you are on and `main~2` is two before the tip of `main`. `HEAD^` means the same as `HEAD~1`.
task.3.summaryItems.2.title: `git rev-parse <rev>` -
task.3.summaryItems.2.text: prints the hash a name resolves to, which is a quick way to check you counted right.
task.3.summaryItems.3.title: Detached `HEAD` -
task.3.summaryItems.3.text: standing on a commit rather than on a branch, so a commit made there would have no name holding on to it.
task.3.summaryClose: Next: what `reset` actually moves - now that you can name the commit to move it to.
concept.gt-detached-head.def: Standing on a commit directly instead of on a branch, so a commit made there has no branch name holding on to it.
